newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock firm accused of "spreading rumours".
newsitem.headline: China stock firm accused of "spreading rumours".

text.p: China's top securities watchdog has criticised one of the country's major broking firms, Jiangsu Securities Co, for "spreading political rumours" in 1996, the China Business Times said on Wednesday.

The China Securities Regulatory Commission said in a circular the securities firm had spread rumours it picked up from foreign media reports, accessed through its computer network, on November 7 and 8 last year, it said.
The company "has recognised the seriousnesss of its mistakes and conducted an internal rectification," the newspaper said without further detail.
Company officials were not available for comment as all securities firms are closed until February 17 for the annual lunar new year holiday.
In China, "political rumours" usually refer to speculation on the health of Chinese leaders or on major policy changes.
